title: Prisma with NextAuth.js / Auth.js
description: Integrate Prisma with NextAuth v5 via @auth/prisma-adapter to manage users, sessions, verification tokens, and OAuth accounts.

data.text: **Auth.js (NextAuth.js v5)** is the premier authentication library for Next.js. It delegates persistence of users, OAuth accounts, and sessions to database adapters. The `@auth/prisma-adapter` package connects Auth.js directly to Prisma models.

data.title: schema.prisma Auth.js Models
data.content: The required schema structure for NextAuth v5 with PostgreSQL.
data.code:
model User {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  name          String?
  email         String?   @unique
  emailVerified DateTime? @map("email_verified")
  image         String?
  accounts      Account[]
  sessions      Session[]

  @@map("users")
}

model Account {
  id                String  @id @default(cuid())
  userId            String  @map("user_id")
  type              String
  provider          String
  providerAccountId String  @map("provider_account_id")
  refresh_token     String? @db.Text
  access_token      String? @db.Text
  expires_at        Int?
  token_type        String?
  scope             String?
  id_token          String? @db.Text
  session_state     String?

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([provider, providerAccountId])
  @@map("accounts")
}

model Session {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  sessionToken String   @unique @map("session_token")
  userId       String   @map("user_id")
  expires      DateTime
  user         User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@map("sessions")
}

model VerificationToken {
  identifier String
  token      String
  expires    DateTime

  @@unique([identifier, token])
  @@map("verification_tokens")
}

data.content: Connecting PrismaAdapter to NextAuth v5 configuration.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `@auth/prisma-adapter` to connect NextAuth v5 with Prisma.
The Auth.js schema requires `User`, `Account`, `Session`, and `VerificationToken` models.
Use JWT session strategy in serverless setups to avoid hitting the database on every HTTP request.
